posts.content_md:
Hello Holographers,

sorry for my simple question, but I couldnt find the answer here: What density (blackness) should a developed plate get in the well-known Pyrogallol developer (10g/l, plus 60g/l Sodium Carbonate)? Same as usual?

The reason is, I tried it this weekend and got promising results (stability and colour seemed perfect!), but it was much too dim again. Exposure was 2sec with my 6mW HeNe, which yielded good results with Dokumol.

The plate didnt get black after 2min development, it only got slightly better after 6min. The solution was used 5-20min after activating.

Thanks for your help!

Max

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
Here is what I do, I calculate the exposure based on the film manufacture's exposure recomendations. I then expose a plate to 1/2 the energy, the proper energy, double the energy and then 4 times the energy. You can do this all on one plate if you wish. Then I drop it in the developer for 1 minute and process. The brightest one become the standard that I then make finer adjustments to. 

It should be noted that lately I have been over exposing and only using 30 seconds in the developer based on some posts be Jeff. I have found this to work well also.
